summary: The bill repeals section 781 of the Continuing Appropriations Act, 2026 (effective November 12, 2025), undoing its amendments to the Agricultural Marketing Act of 1946 on hemp.

scores.thoughts: The bill text contains no provisions related to federal spending, appropriations, or budget allocations. It solely repeals a section of a prior law concerning hemp regulations under the Agricultural Marketing Act.
No tax provisions, rate changes, credits, or revenue measures appear in the bill. It addresses only the repeal of hemp-related amendments to agricultural marketing law.
The legislation does not address healthcare delivery, insurance, public coverage, or medical services. Hemp regulation here is framed strictly as an agricultural marketing matter.
No references to firearms, gun regulations, or Second Amendment issues exist in the bill.
The bill contains nothing related to immigration policy, border enforcement, visas, or pathways to citizenship.
No provisions touch on reproductive rights, abortion access, or related healthcare regulations.
The bill does not address military funding, defense programs, or national security spending.
While hemp can have environmental implications in other contexts, this bill is narrowly focused on repealing marketing amendments and does not engage environmental protections or regulations.
No content relates to welfare programs, food assistance, or social safety net expansions or reductions.
The legislation has no bearing on schools, education funding, school choice, or federal education policy.

The bill repeals amendments to the Agricultural Marketing Act concerning hemp, an agricultural commodity distinct from marijuana under federal law. It does not address drug scheduling, decriminalization, enforcement, or controlled substances policy.
No provisions address sentencing, policing, rehabilitation, or criminal justice reform.
The bill does not engage tariffs, trade agreements, import/export rules, or protectionist measures.
No fiscal policy, deficit reduction, or debt-related measures are present.
The bill contains no language related to LGBTQ+ legal protections or rights.
No provisions address foreign assistance, international aid, or related funding.
The legislation does not touch on voting access, election integrity, voter ID, or electoral reforms.
No content relates to technology regulation, data privacy, or digital oversight.
The bill does not address worker protections, union rights, or labor policy.
No provisions engage religious exemptions, civil rights protections, or anti-discrimination law.
